A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Content can be matched reliably across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of unobserved object detection on RealEstate10k and NYU Depth V2, including quantitative comparisons, ablations, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original evaluations and adds an outdoor scene–object evaluation and a failure breakdown in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The DFM, SDXL, and VLM detection pipelines retain their generation, detection, aggregation, projection, and normalization procedures. Revised SDXL implementation wording does not establish a different model or algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds one outdoor RealEstate10k scene featuring a car, extending the previously indoor evaluation to a limited outdoor scenario. The existing indoor datasets, object categories, and detection tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the existing experiments is unchanged. The outdoor evaluation uses already evaluated models. Its Gemini 1.5 Pro label matches the API specified in Appendix D of both versions, so it does not establish a newly added comparator.

E3.justification: The added outdoor evaluation uses one scene–object pair and reports per-case metrics in Table 7, without the FNR column used in indoor comparisons. Existing indoor preprocessing, thresholds, generation budgets, and metric definitions remain unchanged; newly documented manual checks do not establish a revised labeling procedure.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds an outdoor generalization case study and an attribution of DFM failures to prediction errors versus detector false negatives. Existing pose, sample-count, and prompting ablations and qualitative failure examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same seed and sampling information and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting across scene–object combinations. The new outdoor scores and failure percentages introduce no additional uncertainty estimates, repeated-run reporting, or significance procedures.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports outdoor results, including 2D distance of infinity for DFM versus zero for SDXL and the four VLMs; all have accuracy 0.670. Appendix E also adds the 57% prediction-error versus 43% detector-error breakdown. Existing matched table values differ only through equivalent formatting or rounding.

T1.justification: The spatial-distribution definitions and metric equations (1)–(5) are unchanged. Neither the main text nor appendices introduce or remove substantive mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: defining unobserved object detection, adapting three generative-model families, and benchmarking them with proposed metrics. The conclusion retains the distinction between out-of-frame prediction and DFM's ability to address fully occluded objects.

C2.justification: v3 attributes outdoor DFM difficulties to limited outdoor training and adds retraining-cost and reconstruction-scale caveats. Section 6 removes discussion of task-specific training and consistency–diversity tradeoffs, while retaining the principal prompting, memorization, and inference-time limitations.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents manual annotation checks and the absence of dataset-specific generation tuning. It replaces the promised code/dataset/protocol release with a project-page link for code and protocols, drops the environment-release promise, and revises RunwayML wording to the Diffusers SDXL pipeline. These are documentation changes rather than evidence of reruns.

R1.justification: v3 adds the DL3DV-10K citation for future outdoor and large-scale work and removes Astolfi et al.'s consistency–diversity–realism reference. The main related-work positioning is retained; corrections to the NYU Depth V2 reference concern the same cited work.

P1.justification: There are localized prose edits, a condensed conclusion and future-work discussion, revised affiliation text, and added acknowledgements. The main section sequence and Appendix A–E organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds outdoor Figure 11 and Table 7, relocates pipeline figures and Table 5, and reorders the first two columns of the existing SDXL sample montage with matching labels. Other figures and table structures are substantially retained.

improvement.justification: The outdoor example supplies useful evidence of an applicability boundary, while documented manual checks and code/protocol access instructions modestly improve transparency. Gains are limited: the new failure percentages lack supporting counts, and the statement that prompted SDXL has no failures is unreconciled with retained Figure 6(g) and nonzero FNRs in Tables 14–15. The central experimental evidence remains unchanged.
